personas.name: A screen-reader user filing a complaint
personas.summary: A hypothetical blind resident who uses a screen reader on a phone and wants to report a blocked drain and follow it up.

stages.friction: Finding the correct body may be hard after the reorganisation, and unnamed links would be read aloud only as 'link'.
stages.evidence: Unnamed links or buttons on 56% of audited Bengaluru pages and 65% in Hyderabad.

stages.friction: An undeclared page language can make a screen reader use the wrong pronunciation, and images without alternatives leave gaps.
stages.evidence: The page language is undeclared on 4 of 16 Bengaluru pages and 17 of 23 Hyderabad pages.

stages.friction: A visual CAPTCHA could end the attempt if no audio alternative works.
stages.evidence: CAPTCHA signals on 7 of 40 audited pages. Audio alternatives were not checked.

stages.friction: A field with no label is announced without its purpose.
stages.evidence: Unlabelled form fields on 25% of audited Bengaluru pages and 26% in Hyderabad.

stages.friction: An error may appear only visually, without being announced.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: Status tables and references may be hard to find again by ear.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: There may be no accessible way to confirm the drain was actually cleared.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

personas.name: A resident who reads Urdu, with limited English and Telugu
personas.summary: A hypothetical Hyderabad resident who reads Urdu confidently, has limited English and Telugu, and wants to check a ration card application.

stages.friction: Search results and official names may appear only in English or Telugu.
stages.evidence: Urdu is the mother tongue of 29.5% of GHMC residents in Census 2011.

stages.friction: This resident needs a language control they can recognise, and any Urdu option we found sits on a page with a translation widget.
stages.evidence: Urdu option on 2 of 23 audited Hyderabad pages. Translation widgets appeared on 5, and their output was not assessed.

stages.friction: One-time passwords and error messages may arrive in another language.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: Names and addresses may need English or Telugu spellings that differ from the resident's documents.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: A paid intermediary may be needed, which shifts cost and privacy risk onto the resident.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: Status terms may be unfamiliar even after machine translation.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: The counter staff may or may not be able to help in Urdu.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

personas.name: An older resident who finds complex systems hard to follow
personas.summary: A hypothetical older Bengaluru resident with a smartphone and some memory difficulties, who has received a property tax demand and is unsure what to do.

stages.friction: The first job is working out which of several bodies and addresses is responsible, and old names persist.
stages.evidence: The property tax portal still uses a 'bbmptax' address after the BBMP was replaced. Reorganisation reported in September 2025.

stages.friction: A very long landing page presents many choices before the task can begin.
stages.evidence: Median visible links on audited pages: 63 in Bengaluru and 13 in Hyderabad. Link count is a rough proxy, not a usability score.

stages.friction: OTPs and timeouts create pressure, and losing access to an old phone number can block the task.
stages.evidence: The Bengaluru tax portal has a dedicated 'Change Mobile Number (Old number unavailable)' route, which suggests that this problem occurs.

stages.friction: Legal terms and property identifiers may require documents that are hard to find.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: It may be unclear whether a payment succeeded.
stages.evidence: The portal has separate 'Payment Status' and 'Acknowledgement Print' routes; we did not test how clear they are.

stages.friction: Several reference numbers have to be remembered across systems.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

stages.friction: Finishing may rely on a relative or agent, which is invisible in official records.
stages.evidence: Fieldwork question. We have not observed this step.

language_note: In Census 2011, Kannada was the mother tongue of 42.1% of BBMP-area residents, followed by Tamil (16.3%) and Telugu (13.7%). In the GHMC area it was Telugu (58.5%) and Urdu (29.5%). Mother tongue does not show which scripts a person reads, and many residents are multilingual. These figures show which languages are worth testing, not who is excluded.
